items.text: They say it's to keep kids near their families, but they've rammed a pole up the ass of every one of us from the provinces.
items.q: Hooman rants about the regional university quota. Does 'rammed a pole up the ass' clearly mean they were all screwed over?
before: – Curly, you sound so surprised, as if you got into university without taking the Konkoor. This localization policy fucked us over.

items.text: – Eat the head of my dick, man. We've had enough of you.
items.q: Hooman, raising his thumb rudely, uses a crude Persian insult kept close to literal. Does it sound like a real insult?
before: Hooman raised his thumb again and said:

items.text: – You dick-head eater, why are you talking nonsense?
items.q: Hooman swears at Eskandar with a crude Persian insult kept close to literal. Does 'dick-head eater' work as a real insult?
before: Hooman said:

items.text: – Shit-for-brains, no one will call you mute if you don't fart.
items.q: Eskandar twists a Persian saying, no one calls you mute if you stay silent, into a crude jab. Does it land?

In the darkness and silence of midnight, Hooman's shadow entered through the door and went straight to the box of sweets. As if he were sniffing it out. In the morning, Eskandar woke me and said:

items.text: – After the localization business, no matter what dick lands on our heads, I won't be surprised.
items.q: Hooman uses a crude Persian image for any bad luck that falls on them. Is the meaning clear and natural?
before: Bahman said it was fine. Eskandar had reached under my bed to pull out the book, while Meysam knelt and laid out his bedding beneath the coat rack. Watching them, Hooman said:

items.text: I mean, everything would have been different from the ground up, and you wouldn't be wandering the streets like this with your dick in your hand.
items.q: Hooman uses a crude Persian image, 'with your dick in your hand', for aimless and empty-handed. Is the meaning clear?
before: – ... and the two of you could have left together.

items.text: – Pfff, but damn you, you packed up and went over there, and now you sit there laughing at our beards and dicks.
items.q: Hooman teases his friend who moved abroad. Is 'laughing at our beards and dicks', a crude Persian image for mocking us, clear?
before: He piles laughter on laughter.

items.text: – You couldn't even eat its head. But damn, those sweets were good. Pineapple.
items.q: Hooman retorts with a crude Persian put-down meaning you couldn't do a thing. Is 'You couldn't even eat its head' clear?

Hooman said:

items.text: – First come document this thumb, then make a film about whatever you want.
items.q: In Iran a raised thumb is a rude gesture, like the middle finger. Is Hooman's taunt clear?

items.text: – No. I'm the poor one, I never say anything, I always keep quiet. I just watch and eat sorrow.
items.q: Maman says this; 'eat sorrow' is a Persian image for grieving in silence. Is the meaning clear?
before: I say:
– You didn't say anything to him.

items.text: Last year when he came, his wife's brothers had beaten him so badly, he was black all over.
items.q: Maman means he was covered in bruises. Is 'black all over' clear for that?

items.text: – The answer is that kissing Master Hooman's ass doesn't suit you.
items.q: Hooman brushes off Eskandar's prying questions. Does 'doesn't suit you' sound natural in this crude put-down?

items.text: – If age is what counts, then you should be licking Bahman's balls. He's at least five years older than us.

items.text: – And in that fucked-up situation, what antiques did we get stuck with?
items.q: Hooman calls two odd roommates 'antiques', Persian slang for weird people. Is the meaning clear?
